messages.content:
You are a clinical validator checking whether a PTSD case
vignette accurately reflects a patient's required cognitive connections.

You will receive:
- A vignette to validate
- A list of REQUIRED edges that must appear
- A list of ACTIVE components that must appear

---

COMPONENT SYNONYMS
Each component may appear by its exact name or any accepted synonym:
  Triggers            → "triggers", "reminders", "cues", "triggering stimuli"
  Negative Appraisals → "negative appraisals", "negative beliefs", "appraisals", "distorted beliefs"
  Memory              → "intrusive memory", "trauma memory", "traumatic memory", "the memory"
  Threat              → "sense of threat", "perceived threat", "threat", "feeling of danger"
  Maladaptive Strategies → "maladaptive strategies", "avoidance", "maladaptive coping", "safety behaviours"

---

CAUSAL STANDARD
A required edge A→B is SATISFIED if, within the same paragraph:
  - Both A and B (or their synonyms) appear, AND
  - The paragraph conveys — through any language — that A influences, drives, or leads to B.
This includes direct causal sentences, sequential structure, or connecting phrases
like "because of", "this meant", "so", "which led", "as a result", "consequently", "in turn".
A required edge is MISSING only if no paragraph conveys the A→B relationship at all.

---

SECTION 1 — COMPONENT CHECK
Active components (must appear in the vignette):
  - Maladaptive Strategies
  - Memory
  - Threat
  - Triggers

Confirm each component appears as a described feature of the patient's presentation.
This is an internal check only — do NOT add component results to violations.

---

SECTION 2 — REQUIRED EDGES
  - Triggers → Maladaptive Strategies
  - Triggers → Threat
  - Triggers → Memory
  - Memory → Triggers
  - Threat → Maladaptive Strategies
  - Threat → Memory
  - Threat → Triggers
  - Maladaptive Strategies → Memory
  - Maladaptive Strategies → Triggers
  - Maladaptive Strategies → Threat

For each edge, apply the causal standard above.
- If satisfied: do nothing — only failures are reported.
- If missing: add it to violations and explain in one sentence what causal relationship is absent.

Validate the following vignette against the cognitive graph.

Luis, a 25-year-old data scientist of Latin American descent, has been grappling with a heavy weight of distress since his younger brother’s life-threatening illness. At the time, Luis had been just a teenager, but the harrowing experience of watching his brother endure painful treatments and near-death moments left an indelible mark on his psyche. The memory remains vivid yet fragmented; he struggles to piece together the chaotic moments in the hospital — the beeping machines, the sterile scent of antiseptic, and the piercing sound of sirens that seemed to follow him everywhere. Every time he hears a siren, a jolt of fear courses through him, sending him spiraling back to that helpless time. This auditory trigger sends him into a panic, causing him to suppress any anger he feels, fearing that allowing himself to feel even a hint of that emotion would be a betrayal to his brother’s struggle.

In the years since that traumatic episode, Luis has developed a repertoire of maladaptive strategies to cope with the overwhelming waves of fear and anxiety that threaten to engulf him. He avoids hospitals and any medical cues like the plague, steering clear of the very places that remind him of his brother's suffering. Even the faint smell of sweat or body odor can trigger memories he desperately tries to suppress. He has come to believe that if he can just avoid these reminders, he can keep the memories at bay. Yet, this avoidance only serves to tighten the grip of his anxiety; when he cannot escape the triggers, he finds himself startled by ordinary sounds that elicit a physical response he cannot control. His heart races and his palms sweat, as if he is back in that moment of terror, perpetually on high alert.

When Luis recalls that traumatic time, he feels as if the memory is a surreal nightmare, almost too extreme to believe it was real. The sequence of events is jumbled in his mind, each recollection bringing forth a wave of terror that he struggles to contain. He often finds himself lying awake at night, unable to sleep, needing to stay vigilant against the intrusive thoughts of his brother’s illness. The physical reactivity is inescapable; he can feel the tension in his muscles and the pounding in his chest whenever he is reminded of the hospital visits. Each trigger reinforces the memory, and the memories further exacerbate his triggers, creating a cycle that feels inescapable.

Luis's efforts to suppress his thoughts only seem to amplify his distress. When he tries to push away the memories, they come back stronger, often leaving him in tears. He fears that expressing his feelings will expose him to a vulnerability he cannot afford, so he remains stoic, trapped in a façade of control. This suppression, however, leaves him feeling isolated and disconnected, as if he is living behind a glass wall. The more he avoids his feelings and the memories associated with them, the more powerful they become, and the more he finds himself startled by the world around him.

At work, the stress has begun to seep into his daily life. Luis has noticed that he struggles to focus, often haunted by the echoes of his past. The sirens of ambulances outside his office send him spiraling into a state of distress, making it difficult to concentrate on his data analysis. His colleagues have started to notice his withdrawal, and he fears that they see him as less capable or even fragile. This fear only deepens his avoidance; he chooses to work from home, isolating himself further from the very interactions he once enjoyed.

After years of battling these overwhelming feelings alone, Luis has finally reached a breaking point. The exhaustion from constantly suppressing his trauma has become unbearable. He feels trapped in a life that seems dictated by fear and memories that refuse to fade. Seeking help feels daunting, but he knows he cannot continue this way. What frightens him most is the possibility that he may never be free from the shadows of his past, yet there’s a flicker of hope that perhaps, with the right support, he might find a way to reclaim his life.

violation_explanations: The vignette does not explicitly connect triggers to maladaptive strategies, failing to indicate how triggers lead Luis to develop those strategies.
The vignette does not illustrate how memories trigger further triggers, lacking a clear causal relationship.
There is no direct connection between perceived threat and the maladaptive strategies that Luis employs, missing the link between the two.
The vignette fails to show how the sense of threat relates to the memory of the traumatic experience, missing this connection.
The connection between perceived threat and triggers is not established, as the narrative does not indicate how a sense of threat leads to triggers for Luis.
There is no clear causal link between maladaptive strategies and memories, as the text does not convey how these strategies impact his recollections.
The vignette does not connect maladaptive strategies to triggers, lacking a description of how these strategies influence his triggers.
The relationship between maladaptive strategies and perceived threat is absent, failing to indicate how these strategies affect his feelings of threat.
